changes.unchanged: FFN-only scope; dense layer 0; mandatory RGB >5/255; stable score ranking and spatial ties; fresh attention, residual gates, future and action computation; previous execution optimizations.

paper_alignment.online: Figure 6 and Appendix E.3 specify 16/80/120 with full initialization; corresponding local paper_eval MethodConfig sets reserve_fraction=0.
paper_alignment.fixed80: Appendix C.4 specifies alpha=0, B={80,120} for repeated-input profiling. This is a separate profile, not an unconditional 80-token online budget.
paper_alignment.epsilon: Appendix D.1 relative feature metric and the historical GPU feature selector use a 1e-12 denominator floor.

audit.protocol: Shared weights, fixed per-shape FFN algorithms, seed 42; identical dense history restored before each request outside timing. CPU image/state to denormalized CPU actions, synchronized including cache commits. 30 alternating AB/BA pairs per capacity and fixture, control refresh=80. No compilation or capture during timing. Forced 2F/4F, ten Euler updates. Clocks unlocked, background applications resident. Not closed-loop.
audit.fixture: One request plus synthetic +64 modulo-256 changes in 0/1/12 32x32 RGB tiles. Not the paper recorded observation pairs.

correctness.scope: Equality is across repeated calls with matching capacity/input/restored history. New default policy need not match previous defaults. Dense initialization equals reuse off at 2F/4F/10F.

limitations: One offline input and synthetic RGB tile changes; no natural rollout or task-success evaluation.
Capacity sweep restores dense history before every request. It does not measure long-horizon recursive-cache drift.

Normalized MAE averages all model action coordinates before denormalization, including inactive/padded coordinates. It is not the paper D.3 32x10-coordinate MAE. No monotonic quality benefit is established.
Different capacities use different fixed cuBLASLt plans, so deviations include BF16 kernel-shape rounding effects.
GPU clocks are unlocked and background applications remain resident. Small deltas can reflect scheduling noise; 80-vs80 is a same-configuration timing control, not an optimization.
120-token full refresh still enables reuse bookkeeping; it is not a reuse-off timing baseline.
Current checkpoint and fixtures differ from the historical step-600 paper profiling runtime. Policy alignment does not establish reproduction of paper latency or success rates.
Checkpoint, input fixture and historical source snapshots are not bundled.
